column3: Using hardcoded IP addresses is security-sensitive
column7: ruff S104 flags binding to all interfaces only, not literal IP addresses

column3: Hard-coded credentials are security-sensitive
column7: bandit rules match password-named variables, arguments and defaults; secrets under other names are missed (gitleaks covers known token shapes)

column3: Using pseudorandom number generators (PRNGs) is security-sensitive
column7: S311 flags every use of the random module, which is broader than Sonar but misses other weak generators

column3: Using weak hashing algorithms is security-sensitive
column7: S324 covers hashlib and a few other call forms; other libraries are missed

column3: Formatting SQL queries is security-sensitive
column7: S608 matches string-built SQL by shape; queries assembled across statements are missed

column3: Server certificates should be verified during SSL/TLS connections
column7: S501 flags requests and httpx calls with verify=False; ssl context and other libraries are missed

column3: Weak SSL/TLS protocols should not be used
column7: ruff checks ssl.wrap_socket and PROTOCOL_ constants in direct calls only

column3: Cipher algorithms should be robust
column7: ruff flags a fixed list of weak cipher classes; others are missed

column3: Using shell interpreters when executing OS commands is security-sensitive
column7: ruff flags shell=True and os.system style calls; other shell paths are missed
